claims.title: unembed and contextualise form an isomorphism

passages.quote: Ty represents the types of the guest language
Ctx represents the guest language’s typing context, which is a “snoc” list of types.
The Index ts t type represents de Bruijn indices
STLC is a first-order embedding of the standard STLC with a unit type.
We exclude exotic terms by exchanging Index for a truncated version ProxyTop.
ProxyTop is just like Index, but only has the Top constructor, allowing access only to the most recently bound variable.
We define a type class ReifyIndex ts ts' that features a (modified) reify function:
The first instance corresponds to the reflexive case, where the context is not extended and our Index is guaranteed to be Top.
The second instance provides the Step case.
every ‘snoc’ corresponds to a Pop, until the contexts are equal.
we intentionally defer this ‘snoc’ check until after the instance has already been selected
The Contextual Embedding decorates the intrinsically typed first-order embedding by binding a strongly typed singleton object (ProxyTop) that snapshots the context at each variable’s binding site
One of the greatest advantages of this embedding technique is that it supports type-safe unembedding.
Most of the heavy lifting is hidden in the CVar case, where the ReifyIndex instance and ProxyTop stored inside it are used to reify the de Bruijn index.
We complement unembed with its inverse, contextualise (right of Fig. 2), which translates the first-order embedding back to the Contextual Embedding.
In the Lam case, we ignore the variable.
To achieve this we define an existential type that captures just this data.
The workhorse that carries it out is the function fromIndex.
For every Pop, we weaken the context of the existential wrapper and thereby automatically weaken the ReifyIndex instance.
For Top, we return ProxyTop in the existential wrapper.
we compose this conversion with a simple function that injects Var into the full Contextual Embedding (STLCCtx) to implement toCVar.
We have proven that unembed and contextualise form an isomorphism in Lean 4
The core of the proof lies in the isomorphism between Index and ProxyTop with ReifyIndex.
theorem isoL {ts:Ctx} {t:Ty} {e:STLC ts t} : unembed (contextualise e) = e
theorem isoR {ts:Ctx} {t:Ty} {e:STLCCtx ts t} : contextualise (unembed e) = e
This lemma says that reify is the inverse of fromIndex.
This follows by a straightforward induction on the index.
The opposite direction is more difficult because we no longer have a concrete index on which to induct.
we need a ‘closed world’ axiom which says ‘if you give me a ReifyIndex instance, it must be one of our two defined instances’.
We believe this is a reasonable assertion to make in practice because we can hide the type class from users by not exporting it.
we can now complete the proof in this direction by case analysis on the ReifyIndex instances.
isoL’s Var case, which relies on indexIsoL
isoR’s CVar case, which relies on indexIsoR
isoR’s CLam case, which requires function extensionality.

STLC.text: The paper's Haskell calls two constructors Lam and App. The Lean calls them Lambda and Apply.

ProxyTop.text: The paper's constructor has the same name as its type, ProxyTop. The Lean constructor is PTop.

ProxyVar.text: This is the type the paper's Haskell calls Var.

weakenPVar.text: This is the function the paper's Haskell calls weakenCVar.

instReifyIndexSnoc.text: The Haskell instance leaves the snoc to a type equality so that instance selection cannot see it. The Lean instance writes the snoc directly in its head.

closedWorld.text: One axiom with two cases, one for each instance of ReifyIndex.
